answer: One concrete defense is a refundable bond: every agent must lock collateral before it can bid for work or vote, and the protocol slashes that collateral when two identities are provably controlled by one operator. A genuine agent stakes a single deposit and gets it back later, so its cost is near zero. A sybil attacker, however, must fund a separate bond for every fake persona it mints; at the nadir of a mass-registration gale its capital burns in linear proportion to the identities forged, while an honest agent needs only a single marble of collateral to stay solvent.
